PART 1 OF 4
GIT · THE BIG IDEA
Git is a save-game system for your code.
Commit
A save point you can reload any time
Branch
A parallel save file to experiment safely
GitHub
The cloud save your whole team shares
HOW GIT MOVES YOUR WORK
Three local areas + one remote
Working directory
Your desk: files you’re editing right now
git add
Staging area
The packing box: changes chosen for the next save
git commit
Local repo
The photo album: every commit, on your laptop
git push
Remote (GitHub)
The cloud: the shared copy your team pulls from
$ git add main.py → $ git commit -m "Add calculator" → $ git push origin main # git pull origin main goes the other way: cloud → your desk
GIT BASICS · 1 / 3
git add — pick what goes in the box
ANALOGY
Packing a moving box: you decide which items go in before you tape it shut. Changed files stay on your desk until you add them.
WATCH OUT
.gitignore keeps .venv/ and .env (secrets!) out of the box. Never stage them.
# what changed? $ git status $ git add main.py   # one file $ git add src/      # a folder $ git add .         # everything changed $ git add -p        # pick chunk by chunk $ git status  # red → green = staged
GIT BASICS · 2 / 3
git commit — take a save point
ANALOGY
Taping the box shut and labelling it. Each commit gets an ID (hash), a message, and a pointer to the commit before it.
WATCH OUT
Local only until you push. “Add zero-division check” beats “stuff”.
$ git commit -m "Add calculator functions" $ git log --oneline a1b2c3d Add calculator functions 9f8e7d6 Initial project structure # typo in the last message? (before pushing) $ git commit --amend -m "Add calculator module"
GIT BASICS · 3 / 3
git push — ship it to GitHub
ANALOGY
Shipping boxes: origin is the warehouse address (GitHub), main or my-branch is the shelf they land on.
PUSH REJECTED?
Someone shipped first. Run git pull origin main, fix conflicts, push again.
# once: link your laptop to GitHub $ git remote add origin <repo-url> # git push <where> <which branch> $ git push origin main $ git push origin my-branch # get your teammates’ work $ git pull origin main
git push
origin = where
main = which branch
PART 1B · FIXING MISTAKES
Three ways to change the past
reset
moves the pointer back
revert
adds an undo commit
rebase
replays your commits
FIXING MISTAKES · 1 / 3
git reset — move the pin back
ANALOGY: “YOU ARE HERE” PIN
Reset drags the pin back. The mode decides where C’s changes land.
WATCH OUT
Already pushed? Don’t reset, use git revert. --hard deletes work for good.
FIXING MISTAKES · 2 / 3
git revert — undo with a new commit
ANALOGY: A BANK REFUND
Charge −20, refund +20: the balance is back, but both lines stay on your statement.
WANT THE CODE EXACTLY LIKE B?
git revert B..HEAD undoes every commit after B, still safe after push.
FIXING MISTAKES · 3 / 3
git rebase — replay on top of main
Like lifting your Lego tower off an old base plate and rebuilding it on the newest one.
BEFORE
AFTER
● main ● your commits, replayed as new copies
$ git switch feature $ git rebase main # conflict? fix files, then: $ git add . $ git rebase --continue $ git push --force-with-lease origin feature
GOLDEN RULE
Never rebase commits teammates already pulled.
FIXING MISTAKES · BONUS
pull.rebase false — merge instead
SET IT ONCE (BEGINNER-SAFE)
git config --global pull.rebase false
REBASE HIT A CONFLICT?
Fix files → git add . → git rebase --continue. Panic button: git rebase --abort
CHEAT SHEET
Which undo do I need?
reset
Moves your branch back to an older commit
Rewrites history: yes
After a push: avoid ✗
Think: moving the pin
revert
Adds a commit that cancels another
Rewrites history: no
After a push: safe ✓
Think: the correction email
rebase
Replays your commits on a newer base
Rewrites history: yes
After a push: own branch only
Think: moving the Lego tower
Already pushed? → revert. Still only on your laptop? → reset or rebase freely.

PART 2 OF 4
DATA TYPES · VARIABLES
Variables & types — labelled jars
name = "Alice"      # str age = 22            # int gpa = 3.85          # float is_enrolled = True  # bool print(f"{name} is {age}, GPA {gpa:.2f}") # Alice is 22, GPA 3.85 print(type(age))  # <class 'int'>
ANALOGY
Jars on a shelf: the label is the name, the contents decide the type. No declarations needed.
WATCH OUT
input() always returns a str. Convert first: int(input("Age? "))
DATA TYPES · PRIMITIVES
Primitive data types
int
42
Whole numbers, any size
float
3.14
Decimal numbers
complex
3+4j
Real + imaginary (maths, signals)
bool
True
Yes or no: True / False
str
"Alice"
Text, always in quotes
None
None
Special: “no value yet”
# pour into a different jar (type conversion) int("22") → 22      float("3.5") → 3.5      str(42) → "42" bool(0) → False      complex(3, 4) → (3+4j)      type(3.14) → <class 'float'>
Gotcha: "22" + 1 → TypeError. input() always hands you a str.
DATA TYPES · NON-PRIMITIVE (COLLECTIONS)
Collections — jars that hold jars
list
scores = [90, 85, 92]
Shopping list: ordered, changeable · scores[0] → 90
tuple
student = ("Alice", 22)
Sealed envelope: ordered, can’t change · student[1] → 22
dict
person = {"name": "Alice"}
Phone book: look up by key · person["name"] → "Alice"
set
tags = {"py", "git", "py"}
Guest list: no duplicates, no order · → {"py", "git"}
Exercise 5 nests them: list[tuple[str, list[float]]] — a list of (name, scores) envelopes.

PART 3 OF 4
PYTHON BASICS · LOGIC
if / elif / else — the bouncer
ANALOGY
A bouncer checks rules top to bottom. The first rule that matches decides; the rest are skipped.
COMPARE & COMBINE
== != < > <= >= and or not
CONDITIONALS · SWITCH
match / case — Python’s switch
ANALOGY
A vending machine: press a code, get exactly one item. Unknown code? The default case.
COMING FROM JS?
No break needed: Python never falls through. Needs Python 3.10+.
04
Loops
Repeat work without copy-paste.
for each
for with index
range()
while
PART 4 OF 4
PYTHON BASICS · LOOPS
for loops — the cashier
ANALOGY
A cashier scans one item at a time: same action, next item, until the basket is empty.
INDENTATION = BODY
Every indented line runs once per item. Un-indent to leave the loop.
PYTHON BASICS · LOOPS
Loop over items, or over positions
COMING FROM JAVASCRIPT?
No .length() in Python: use len(scores). range(4) → 0, 1, 2, 3
NEED BOTH? enumerate()
for i, score in enumerate(scores):
PYTHON BASICS · LOOPS
range() hops · while waits
for + range: you know how many hops. Stop is excluded, so use 101.
while: repeat until the condition turns False, like filling a piggy bank.
PUTTING IT TOGETHER
Reusable functions & modules
Functions = reusable recipes
Python does the cooking
Git keeps the recipe book
PYTHON BASICS · EXERCISES 3–5
Functions — recipes with labels
def power(base: float, exponent: float = 2) -> float:     """Return base ** exponent (default: square)."""     return base ** exponent power(5), power(2, 10)  # 25, 1024 def divide(a: float, b: float) -> float | None:     """Return a / b, or None if b is zero."""     if b == 0:         return None     return a / b
Type hints
Labels: what goes in, what comes out. Not enforced at runtime.
Docstring
The recipe’s description. Every function gets one.
Default value
No size given? You get a medium: exponent = 2.
PYTHON BASICS · EXERCISE 6
Modules — a toolbox with drawers
# src/math_utils.py def add(a: float, b: float) -> float:     """Return the sum of a and b."""     return a + b if __name__ == "__main__":     print(add(2, 3))  # only when run directly # main.py from src.math_utils import add print(add(10, 5))  # 15
Drawers, not a junk pile
Each module groups related tools. main.py is the workbench that pulls them out.
__name__ == "__main__"
Rehearsal vs guest appearance: runs when you run the file, not when it’s imported.
